title: A Dataset and Model for Imputing Water Surface Elevation on a Large and Extremely Sparse Spatiotemporal Graph
abstract: arXiv:2609.11580v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continuous monitoring of water surface elevation across river networks is critical for flood forecasting, water resource management, and understanding the global water cycle. Yet, the scarcity of in situ gauges across much of the globe constrains the development of reliable modeling frameworks. Satellite altimetry has the potential to alleviate this problem but its use is currently hindered by sparse temporal coverage. To this end, we introduce AmazonSWE, a dataset for training and evaluating large-scale spatiotemporal graph imputation methods that integrates processed satellite altimetry measurements from a range of sources, including the recent wide-swath SWOT sensor. The dataset covers over 19K river sections and 10 years (2016-2026) in the Amazon river basin, with in situ gauges held out for evaluation. translated_title: 一个用于在大型且极度稀疏的时空图上进行水面高程插补的数据集与模型
translated_abstract: 对河流网络中水面高程的连续监测对于洪水预报、水资源管理以及理解全球水循环至关重要。然而，全球大部分地区原位水文观测站的稀缺限制了可靠建模框架的开发。卫星测高技术有潜力缓解这一问题，但目前其应用受到时间覆盖稀疏的制约。为此，我们推出了AmazonSWE，这是一个用于训练和评估大规模时空图插补方法的数据集，它整合了来自多种来源的经过处理的卫星测高测量数据，包括最新的宽幅SWOT传感器。该数据集覆盖了亚马逊流域超过1.9万个河段以及10年（2016-2026）的数据，并保留了原位水文站数据用于评估。除了贡献一个具有潜在社会影响的新颖现实应用场景外，AmazonSWE还引入了重大的技术……
tldr: 该论文提出了AmazonSWE数据集，整合多源卫星测高数据（包括SWOT传感器），覆盖亚马逊流域超过1.9万个河段和10年时间跨度，用于训练和评估大规模时空图上的水面高程插补方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AmazonSWE, a dataset integrating multi-source satellite altimetry data (including the SWOT sensor) covering over 19K river sections across 10 years in the Amazon basin, for training and evaluating large-scale spatiotemporal graph imputation of water surface elevation.
